findings.title: Conditional passkeys UI is no longer offered during re-authentication because fillContextForm is gated on a non-null user
findings.body: In UsernamePasswordForm.authenticate(), the call to webauthnAuth.fillContextForm(context) was moved outside the else branch and is now guarded by isConditionalPasskeysEnabled(context.getUser()), which returns false whenever context.getUser() is null. During a re-authentication (e.g. OIDC prompt=login) the user is not yet set in the authentication context when the login form is first rendered, so the WebAuthn conditional UI attributes (challenge, RP ID, ENABLE_WEBAUTHN_CONDITIONAL_UI) are never set on the form. The browser therefore never invokes navigator.credentials.get() with the conditional mediation, and passwordless passkey re-authentication on the username/password form is impossible. The same gating in challenge(context, error, field) (line 137) means that after a failed password attempt during re-authentication the conditional UI is also not re-armed. The guard should be based on webauthnAuth != null && webauthnAuth.isPasskeysEnabled() (as before), not on the presence of a user in the context.

findings.title: UsernameForm skips the username step during re-authentication when conditional passkeys are enabled, breaking the username+password+passkey flow
findings.body: UsernameForm.authenticate() now skips rendering the username form (context.success()) whenever context.getUser() != null && !isConditionalPasskeysEnabled(). The intent is to allow passkey re-authentication, but the condition is inverted with respect to the surrounding logic: when conditional passkeys ARE enabled the form is skipped entirely, so a user who must re-authenticate with username+password (e.g. a non-discoverable key, or a user without a passkey) is never asked for their username and the subsequent PasswordForm cannot validate anything. Conversely, when passkeys are disabled the old behavior (skip when user is set) is preserved. The check should be !isConditionalPasskeysEnabled() only for deciding whether passkeys can bypass the form; the skip should still happen when the user has no usable passkey path. As written, the separate UsernameForm + PasswordForm flow cannot complete a password re-authentication when the PASSKEYS feature and realm passkeys are enabled.

findings.title: Refactor to shouldShowWebAuthnAuthenticators() changes behavior when the method is overridden to return false but a user is present
findings.body: fillContextForm() previously branched on user != null to decide whether to build the WebAuthnAuthenticatorsBean (the list of allowed authenticators for a 2FA-style identified user). It now calls shouldShowWebAuthnAuthenticators(context), whose default implementation is context.getUser() != null, but WebAuthnConditionalUIAuthenticator overrides it to always return false. In WebAuthnConditionalUIAuthenticator.fillContextForm() (which calls super.fillContextForm()), this means that even when a user IS identified in the context (re-authentication with a known user), the ALLOWED_AUTHENTICATORS attribute is never set and isUserIdentified is always false. For the conditional UI this is intentional, but the base-class contract is now misleading: any other subclass overriding shouldShowWebAuthnAuthenticators() to false while still wanting per-user authenticator lists would silently lose them. More importantly, the new method name and javadoc ('true if the available webauthn authenticators should be shown on the screen') does not match what it actually controls (whether the per-user allowed-authenticators list is populated), which invites future misuse. The override in WebAuthnConditionalUIAuthenticator should instead override a narrower hook or the base method should be documented/renamed to reflect that it gates the allowed-authenticators list.

findings.title: createErrorResponse() calls setupReauthenticationInUsernamePasswordFormError() unconditionally, hiding the username field even for first-time logins
findings.body: WebAuthnConditionalUIAuthenticator.createErrorResponse() now calls AuthenticatorUtils.setupReauthenticationInUsernamePasswordFormError(context) on every WebAuthn error rendered through the conditional UI. That helper sets LoginFormsProvider.USERNAME_HIDDEN=true and REGISTRATION_DISABLED=true whenever the auth note USER_SET_BEFORE_USERNAME_PASSWORD_AUTH is 'true'. The note is only set by UsernamePasswordForm when a user is already in the context, so for a normal first-time login the helper is a no-op; however, the helper is invoked before fillContextForm(context) and before errorChallenge.apply(context), and it mutates the shared form provider obtained from context.form(). Because the same LoginFormsProvider instance is reused for the error challenge, any code path that reaches createErrorResponse() with the re-authentication note set (e.g. a passkey error during re-authentication on the username/password form) will hide the username field and disable registration on the error page. That is the desired behavior for re-authentication, but the method is placed in the generic WebAuthn error path rather than in the username/password-specific error challenge, so any future caller of WebAuthnConditionalUIAuthenticator that is not the username/password form (the class is designed to be reusable via the errorChallenge function) would incorrectly get username-hiding/registration-disabling attributes applied to an unrelated form. The call belongs in the errorChallenge lambda supplied by UsernamePasswordForm, not in the generic authenticator.

findings.title: Static import of USER_SET_BEFORE_USERNAME_PASSWORD_AUTH from AbstractUsernameFormAuthenticator creates a package cycle and widens a constant's visibility unnecessarily
findings.body: AuthenticatorUtils (in org.keycloak.authentication.authenticators.util) now statically imports AbstractUsernameFormAuthenticator.USER_SET_BEFORE_USERNAME_PASSWORD_AUTH from org.keycloak.authentication.authenticators.browser. This introduces a dependency from the generic util package back into the browser authenticator package, and it required changing the constant from protected to public in AbstractUsernameFormAuthenticator (line 58) solely to make it visible across packages. A public mutable-looking constant on an abstract authenticator class is a wider API surface than needed; the constant is an internal auth-note key. The cleaner approach is to move the constant (or a copy) into AuthenticatorUtils itself or into a shared constants class, and have AbstractUsernameFormAuthenticator reference it from there, avoiding both the package cycle and the visibility widening.

findings.title: reauthenticationOfUserWithoutPasskey asserts absence of the webauthn form with a try/catch that swallows all exceptions, making the assertion ineffective
findings.body: The test reauthenticationOfUserWithoutPasskey verifies that the webauthn button is absent by calling driver.findElement(By.xpath("//form[@id='webauth']")) inside a try block and catching Exception, with a fail() only if findElement returns normally. Selenium's findElement throws NoSuchElementException when the element is absent, so the catch block is the expected path; however, catching the broad Exception type also swallows any other failure (e.g. StaleElementReferenceException, WebDriverException, or a page not fully loaded) and treats it as success. If the page is in an unexpected state or the driver errors for an unrelated reason, the test will pass even though the webauthn form might actually be present. The assertion should use a proper negative assertion such as assertThrows(NoSuchElementException.class, () -> driver.findElement(...)) or a Hamcrest matcher on findElements(...).isEmpty(), and the same pattern is repeated at line 312 for the re-authentication page.

findings.title: webauthnLoginWithExternalKey_reauthenticationWithPasswordOrPasskey submits a password without a username during re-authentication and relies on a hidden username field
findings.body: In webauthnLoginWithExternalKey_reauthenticationWithPasswordOrPasskey, after triggering re-authentication with prompt=login, the test calls loginPage.login(getPassword("test-user@localhost")) (line 377) and later loginPage.login(getPassword(USERNAME)) (line 410) with only a password argument. The single-argument login() overload submits only the password field, assuming the username is pre-filled/hidden. This works only if the form correctly sets USERNAME_HIDDEN and pre-populates the username, which is exactly the behavior changed by this PR (setupReauthenticationInUsernamePasswordFormError). If the re-authentication form regression (username not hidden / not pre-filled) occurs, the test would submit an empty username and fail with a confusing 'Invalid username or password' error rather than clearly asserting the re-authentication form state. The test should explicitly assert that the username field is hidden and contains the expected user (e.g. via loginPage.getAttemptedUsername() or by checking the hidden input value) before submitting the password-only login, so that a regression in the re-authentication form setup is caught with a clear message.

findings.title: PasskeysUsernameFormTest still asserts that the webauthn form is absent after username entry, contradicting the new behavior where conditional passkeys remain enabled
findings.body: In passwordLoginWithNonDiscoverableKey, after the user enters a valid username on the UsernameForm, the test asserts Assert.assertThrows(NoSuchElementException.class, () -> driver.findElement(By.xpath("//form[@id='webauth']"))) (line 202), i.e. that the webauthn conditional UI form is NOT present on the subsequent password page. However, the PR's stated goal (and the corresponding change in PasskeysOrganizationAuthenticationTest, which now asserts the form IS present) is that passkeys remain enabled during the username/password flow even after the username is known. The UsernameForm+PasswordForm split flow uses PasswordForm, which does not embed the WebAuthnConditionalUIAuthenticator, so the webauthn form may legitimately be absent here; but the test does not document why this flow differs from the UsernamePasswordForm flow, and the assertion will break if PasswordForm is later changed to support conditional passkeys. At minimum the test should comment why the webauthn form is expected to be absent in this split-form flow, otherwise a future change that enables passkeys on PasswordForm will produce a confusing failure.
